- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is high or trending upward.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods; raise forecasts when sentiment is low or trending downward.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes; smooth out forecast overshoots by reducing magnitude of subsequent days after a spike.
- Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above or below recent 5-10 day average, adjust toward historical mean or recent trend.
- For short-term (1-7 day) forecasts, align with sentiment direction; for longer (14+ day) forecasts, dampen sentiment-driven extremes.
- When sentiment drops sharply, reduce forecast volatility and avoid downward corrections unless confirmed by price action.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed, favor conservative mid-range forecasts; avoid extreme highs or lows unless supported by strong technical or macro signals.
